title: The Swing

caption: This painting was a scandal. Find the man in the bushes. #art #arthistory #painting #oilpainting #museum
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-11 (Wikipedia, citing the Wallace Collection): c. 1767-68, Wallace Collection; French title 'Les Hasards heureux de l'escarpolette' (The Happy Accidents of the Swing); Collé's memoirs: a courtier asked Gabriel François Doyen for his mistress on a swing pushed by a bishop; Doyen refused and sent him to Fragonard, who painted a layman instead; young man hidden in the bushes; smiling older man in the shadows pulls the ropes; she flings off her shoe; putto statue with finger to its lips above the young man; small white dog barking; cleaned in 2021.
That the older man doesn't notice the lover is the usual reading, not a documented fact; the slide says 'doesn't seem to'.

slides.headline: This painting was a scandal. Can you see why?
Paris, 1767
slides.text: A courtier wanted a painting of his mistress on a swing. The first painter he asked said no. Fragonard said yes.

slides.headline: Up on the swing
slides.text: She flies through the air in pink silk, laughing, legs kicked high.

slides.headline: And then her shoe flies off
slides.text: An accident? The original title says it all: The Happy Accidents of the Swing.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, in the bushes
slides.text: A young man lies hidden in the roses, looking up. From down there, he has the best view in the garden.

slides.headline: But someone saw him
slides.text: Above him, a stone cupid holds a finger to its lips. Shh.

slides.headline: And who is pushing?
slides.text: In the shadows, a smiling older man pulls the ropes. He doesn't seem to notice the bushes.

slides.headline: Only the dog barks
slides.text: A little white dog yaps at the whole scene. Nobody listens.

slides.headline: His first request was worse
slides.text: The courtier wanted a bishop pushing the swing. Fragonard changed that one detail and kept the rest. Would you have dared?
